_readme: Approved variant questions for Chapters 1 and 10 (2 per section). Options are kept close in length so the longest option is not a giveaway; the correct option is not systematically longer.

quizzes.question: Before touching Bitcoin at all, which older question does the introduction say we must answer?
options: How do computers store and send information
Why money exists in the first place
Which banks keep money the safest

quizzes.question: Over how long does the introduction say you will build up your understanding of money?
options: The next three weeks of classes
The next twenty weeks of the year
The next ten weeks of the course

quizzes.question: Which everyday examples does the lesson use to show how much of life runs on money working?
options: The taxi you took, the airtime you bought, money family sends
Stock market prices, government bond yields and central bank rates
Gold mining output, oil trading volumes and global shipping costs

quizzes.question: What assumption does the lesson say most people never question?
options: That banks are open and ready to help every weekday
That prices stay the same from one year to the next
That money works the way it is supposed to work

quizzes.question: One discussion question compares two currencies in two places. Which one?
options: Why the rand and the dollar are both printed on paper in most countries of the world
Why the rand is worth something different in Cape Town than the dollar in New York
Why the dollar can be spent in Cape Town but the rand cannot be spent there

quizzes.question: One discussion question is about our parents. What does it ask?
options: Why they chose to keep their savings at a bank and not at home in a safe place
Why they prefer buying in shops rather than at the local street markets and stalls
Why they trade hours of their time for money, not for what they need directly

quizzes.question: What bigger question does the final chapter step back to ask?
options: How to buy your first bitcoin at the lowest price
Why any of this actually matters for your life
Which country adopted Bitcoin first

quizzes.question: What does the activity before the chapter ask you to imagine?
options: Your school results one year from now, once all of your exams are finished
Your future job at a big bank in the heart of a busy city centre
Your own community in five or ten years if Bitcoin adoption kept growing

quizzes.question: What do supporters of Central Bank Digital Currencies point to?
options: Complete privacy for every single transaction made by the public
Removing central banks from the financial system entirely
Efficiency and financial inclusion for the unbanked

quizzes.question: How does the section say we should treat the supporters' and the critics' concerns?
options: Take both seriously rather than dismissing either side
Accept the supporters' view and set the critics' concerns aside
Reject every digital currency that a government may issue

quizzes.question: Which of these is named as a real tension in this discussion?
options: Financial privacy versus faster payments for every customer
Financial privacy versus lower bank fees for small customers
Financial privacy versus fighting crime and tax evasion

quizzes.question: What is the central question of this class discussion?
options: Which country has the strongest central bank
Do you have the right to control your own money
How many bitcoin each person should own

quizzes.question: What does the section say about Bitcoin's supply?
options: A committee adjusts the supply every year so that it matches what people demand
The largest mining companies decide how much of it will exist in future
It is fixed and verifiable, so no institution can quietly inflate it away

quizzes.question: Where does the section point to real-world usability that is more than a distant idea?
options: A payment system run by the national central bank
Our own EkasiPay merchant network
Bitcoin ATMs in every large shopping mall

quizzes.question: According to the section, how do most people think about money when they start the course?
options: As something fixed and given, just how things are
As something only banks and governments are able to understand
As a tool that will soon disappear completely from daily life

quizzes.question: Who does the section say to talk to about your certificate and what comes next?
options: The manager of your nearest bank branch in town
Sassa, including about the Postgraduate track
The company that made your phone or your wallet app
